info.title: DEX Bridge
info.summary: Poll a Royal Vendors RVV NG over DEX/UCS and return audit data.

get.description: Liveness, plus the facts an operator most often needs to confirm.

post.description:
Read the vending machine's audit data and return it verbatim.

The response body is the EVA-DTS document the machine produced -- `DXS`
through `DXE`, `G85` checksum intact -- and nothing else. Parsing it is
yours to do.

A read takes about 8.5 seconds of live serial conversation at 9600 baud.
Results are shared for 30 seconds, so a burst of callers produces one
conversation with the machine rather than one each; when that happens you
get the same document back with `X-Poll-Cached: true`. Polling in a loop
gains you nothing and is unkind to a machine that is in service.

`?device_id=` selects a machine when there is more than one. There is one.

200.description: The raw EVA-DTS document, exactly as the machine sent it.

get.summary: List stored polls in a date range
get.description:
List the stored polls between `start` and `end`, oldest first.

Both dates are **required and inclusive**. Pass `YYYY-MM-DD` for whole days
(`end=2026-09-21` covers all of the 21st), or a full ISO 8601 timestamp for
an exact window.

You get identifiers and timestamps only. Fetch the document itself from
`/api/v1/history/{session_id}/raw` -- it is the same EVA-DTS text the
machine produced, and parsing it is still yours to do.

Polling the machine is rate-limited by a 30-second cache; this is not, so
build against history rather than hammering `/api/v1/poll`.

get.description:
The stored EVA-DTS document for one poll, verbatim.

Identical in form to what `/api/v1/poll` returns, but read from history
instead of the machine -- so it costs nothing and is always available.

200.description: The raw EVA-DTS document, exactly as the machine sent it.

get.description:
Every product you can put in a purchase request.

A product here is only a description. How many come in a pack, and which
store to buy at, you say on each purchase request. A product missing from
this list cannot be ordered; ask for it with `POST /api/v1/product-requests`.
The selection codes your team owns. Purchase requests may only name these.

403.description: Needs a team key, not the instructor's.

post.summary: Ask for your slots to be restocked
post.description:
Submit a purchase request for slots your team owns.

A request describes the machine you want: for each slot, what goes in it
and what it sells for. Say whether it is an `off_cycle` (mid-week)
restock. Each line fills one slot, and is either:

* `"source": "purchase"` -- buy `primary`, or `alternate` instead if the
  primary cannot be found. Each says which `store` to buy at (`Walmart`,
  `Costco`, `Amazon` or `BJs`, spelled exactly so), how many `packs`,
  `units_per_pack` -- what one of those packs holds -- and the
  `max_price_per_pack` the stocker may pay. An Amazon choice needs the
  product `url`; or
* `"source": "back_stock"` -- load `units` of a product from your team's
  back stock. Nothing checks here that you have them: that is yours to know.

Every choice, including a load, carries the `sale_price` you want the slot
set to if that product goes in. Money is in dollars, as a number or a
string: `2.95` or `"2.95"`. Sale prices go in steps of 0.05.

**Changing what is in a slot must be deliberate.** Set `change_product` to
`true` on any choice that is not what the slot holds now, and leave it
`false` on one that is. Getting it wrong either way is refused.

The request starts `pending`. Read it back from
`/api/v1/purchase-requests/{id}`: it stays `pending` until the stocker
marks it complete, then shows what was bought, paid, loaded and pulled.

**Your team pays for it.** A request whose most it could cost -- every
line at its `max_price_per_pack` -- is more than your team has available
is refused with `insufficient_funds`. It is kept, as `rejected`, under the
`id` returned. Available means your cash, less what your open requests
could still cost, less the sales tax you owe. A second such refusal in one
day (midnight to midnight, Eastern) stops your team submitting until
midnight (`submissions_locked`).

Per-line error types: `duplicate_slot`, `unknown_slot`, `slot_not_owned`,
`unknown_sku`, `product_not_orderable`, `alternate_same_as_primary`,
`unacknowledged_product_change`, `unexpected_product_change`.

403.description: Needs a team key, not the instructor's.

422.description: `invalid_lines`: one or more lines were refused. Every problem is listed in `items`, each with its own `error_type`, so you can fix them all at once. (A body that does not match the schema at all gets FastAPI's standard validation error instead.) `insufficient_funds`: your team cannot afford it; it was kept as rejected under `id`.

429.description: `too_many_open_requests`: wait for earlier ones to be decided. `submissions_locked`: two refusals for insufficient funds today; try after `next_submission_from`.

get.summary: Where a purchase request has got to
get.description:
One of your team's purchase requests.

Until the stocker marks it complete you get `pending` and nothing more.
Once it is complete you get `door_opened_at` and `door_closed_at` -- when
the machine was open for the restock, which is how you tell a vend of the
old product from one of the new on a slot that changed -- and every slot,
what was asked for, and a
`receipt`: what was bought, the amount paid (`total_paid` is exact;
`unit_cost_paid` is per unit, to four places), how many were dropped or
broken on the way (`units_lost`, with a `loss_note`), how many went into
the slot, how many went to your back stock, and how many of the old
product were pulled out if the slot changed product.

A fulfilled request can still change: anything a line stocked that is
later found broken or missing, in the coil or in your back stock, is added
to that line's `later_losses`. Re-read your recent requests to keep your
own count right.

200.description: `{id, status: "pending", created_at}` until it is marked complete; `{id, status: "rejected", created_at, decision_note}` if it was turned down; otherwise the full listing below.

404.description: No such request for your team.

403.description: Needs a team key, not the instructor's.

post.summary: Ask for a product to be added to the catalog
post.description:
Propose a drink for the catalog.

This adds nothing on its own and orders nothing. If it is approved, the
product appears in `GET /api/v1/products` under the SKU shown on this
request, and you order it with a purchase request like anything else. The
name and SKU it is added under may differ from what you proposed.

403.description: Needs a team key, not the instructor's.

429.description: `too_many_open_requests`: wait for earlier ones to be decided.

get.summary: Whether a product request was approved
get.description: One of your team's product requests: pending, approved with its SKU, or rejected.

404.description: No such request for your team.

403.description: Needs a team key, not the instructor's.

post.summary: Check your team's books (once a day)
post.description:
Send your team's figures as of one poll; hear whether each is close enough.

You report four things as of the poll named in `as_of`: `cash` on hand,
`sales_tax_owed`, the units in every `coil` your team owns, and the units
of each product in your `back_stock`. Each comes back `within` or
`outside`. That is all it will ever tell you: not which way you are off,
not by how much, not which slot.

**One check per team per day** (midnight to midnight, Eastern). A request
refused before the check is made -- a malformed body, a slot you do not
own, a poll not yet in the books -- does not use it up.

403.description: Needs a team key, not the instructor's.

409.description: `not_reconciled_yet`: that poll is not in the books yet; polls are folded in on the hour. `tracking_not_started`: the project's books have not begun.

422.description: `invalid_coil`, `unknown_sku`, `before_tracking_start`: fix and resend. (A body that does not match the schema gets FastAPI's standard validation error.) None of these uses up your check.

units.title: Units
units.description: Units to take from your back stock.

sale_price.title: Sale Price
sale_price.description: What a customer pays at the machine for this product, in dollars, tax included, in steps of 0.05. What you want the slot set to.

max_price_per_pack.title: Max Price Per Pack
max_price_per_pack.description: Null on requests made before it existed.

sale_price.title: Sale Price
sale_price.description: Null on requests made before it existed.

uptime_seconds.title: Uptime Seconds
uptime_seconds.description: Service uptime in seconds. Kept numeric so clients can compute with it.

host_uptime_seconds.title: Host Uptime Seconds
host_uptime_seconds.description: Seconds since the Pi booted; null where unavailable.

host_uptime.title: Host Uptime
host_uptime.description: Host uptime, human readable. Differs from service uptime when the container restarted without the Pi rebooting -- or vice versa.

transmit_enabled.title: Transmit Enabled
transmit_enabled.description: False means the service can listen and record but cannot drive the line.

api_key_required.title: Api Key Required
api_key_required.description: True when any credential is configured, in which case every route except this one needs an X-API-Key.

instructor_key_configured.title: Instructor Key Configured
instructor_key_configured.description: Whether a privileged key exists. While false, force, a resetting read and the guarded routes are refused to everyone.

student_groups.title: Student Groups
student_groups.description: Labels of the configured student groups. Labels only -- never the keys themselves, since this route is deliberately unauthenticated.

index.title: Index
index.description: Position of the line in the request, from 0.

sale_price.title: Sale Price
sale_price.description: Null on requests made before it existed.

name.title: Name
name.description: What it is, e.g. 'Coca-Cola Zero Sugar 20 oz bottle'.

size.title: Size
size.description: Size and container, e.g. '20 oz bottle', '12 oz can'.

line.title: Line
line.description: The product line it belongs to, e.g. 'Coca-Cola'.

note.title: Note
note.description: Why, or where you have seen it sold.

product.description: What was added to the catalog, once approved. May differ from the request.

store.title: Store
store.description: Where to buy it. Exactly one of these spellings.

units_per_pack.title: Units Per Pack
units_per_pack.description: Vendable units in one of those packs, e.g. 12 for a 12-pack.

pack_description.title: Pack Description
pack_description.description: What to look for on the shelf, e.g. '12-pack, 20 oz bottles'.

max_price_per_pack.title: Max Price Per Pack
max_price_per_pack.description: The most the stocker may pay for one of these packs, in dollars. Purchases are tax-exempt, so this is the shelf price.

url.title: Url
url.description: The product page. Required when the store is Amazon, and must be an Amazon link.

sale_price.title: Sale Price
sale_price.description: What a customer pays at the machine for this product, in dollars, tax included, in steps of 0.05. What you want the slot set to.

change_product.title: Change Product
change_product.description: Must be true if this product is not what the slot holds now, and false if it is. An empty slot accepts either.

alternate.description: Bought instead if the primary cannot be found.

off_cycle.title: Off Cycle
off_cycle.description: True for a mid-week restock outside the regular weekly cycle.

door_opened_at.title: Door Opened At
door_opened_at.description: When the stocker opened the machine for this restock (ISO 8601, UTC). A vend before this was of whatever the slot held before; one after `door_closed_at` is of what the receipt says was loaded. Null when nothing went into or out of a coil, and on requests completed before this was recorded.

door_closed_at.title: Door Closed At
door_closed_at.description: When the stocker closed the machine again (ISO 8601, UTC). See door_opened_at.

PurchaseRequestDetail.title: PurchaseRequestDetail
PurchaseRequestDetail.description: A completed request: every line, and what happened to it.

id.title: Id
id.description: On `insufficient_funds`: the refused request, kept as rejected.

next_submission_from.title: Next Submission From
next_submission_from.description: On `submissions_locked`: when your team may submit again.

PurchaseRequestPending.title: PurchaseRequestPending
PurchaseRequestPending.description: What a team sees until its request is marked complete.

sku.title: Sku
sku.description: What was bought or loaded; null when unavailable.

store.title: Store
store.description: Where it was actually bought; null unless something was bought.

units_per_pack.title: Units Per Pack
units_per_pack.description: What the packs actually bought held, which may differ from the request.

total_paid.title: Total Paid
total_paid.description: Exact amount on the store receipt, as a decimal string. Authoritative.

unit_cost_paid.title: Unit Cost Paid
unit_cost_paid.description: total_paid / units_bought to four places, for cost of goods. Units times this can differ from total_paid by under a cent.

units_lost.title: Units Lost
units_lost.description: Units dropped or broken before they reached the coil. Out of what was bought, or out of your back stock for a load; already paid for.

loss_note.title: Loss Note
loss_note.description: What happened to them, when anything was lost.

later_losses.title: Later Losses
later_losses.description: Units of what this line stocked found broken or missing afterwards, in the coil or in your back stock, oldest first. Grows after the request is fulfilled: read it again to keep your count right.

units_pulled.title: Units Pulled
units_pulled.description: Units of the old product taken out in a swap.

slots.title: Slots
slots.description: Selection codes this team may request against.

as_of.title: As Of
as_of.description: The `session_id` of the poll your figures are as of, from `GET /api/v1/history`. Everything up to and including that poll counts; nothing after it.

coil.title: Coil
coil.description: Units in each coil your team owns, by slot. Every slot you own, and only those.

back_stock.title: Back Stock
back_stock.description: Units of each product in your back stock, by SKU. A product left out counts as 0.

as_of_time.title: As Of Time
as_of_time.description: When that poll was taken (ISO 8601, UTC).

next_check_from.title: Next Check From
next_check_from.description: Midnight Eastern, when your next check is allowed.
